properties.name: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in R
properties.description: Comprehensive introduction to modern statistical learning methods including regression, classification, resampling, model selection, tree-based methods, support vector machines, clustering, and deep learning. Emphasizes practical applications with R.

properties.name: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
properties.definition: Fundamental tradeoff in model complexity: simple models have high bias (underfitting) but low variance; complex models have low bias but high variance (overfitting). The goal is to minimize total error = Bias² + Variance + Irreducible Error.
properties.interpretation_guide: If training error is low but test error is high, model has high variance (overfitting). If both are high, model has high bias (underfitting).

properties.name: Training/Test Split
properties.definition: Dividing data into training set (to fit model) and test set (to evaluate performance). Prevents overfitting by evaluating on unseen data.
properties.interpretation_guide: Never use test set for model selection or tuning. Use validation set or cross-validation for that.

properties.name: K-Fold Cross-Validation
properties.description: Divide data into K folds, train on K-1 folds, test on remaining fold, repeat K times. Average the K test errors for final estimate.
properties.interpretation_guide: K=5 or K=10 are common choices. LOOCV (K=n) has low bias but high variance. K=10 is a good balance.

properties.name: Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV)
properties.description: Special case of K-fold CV where K=n. Each observation is used once as test set.
properties.interpretation_guide: Computationally expensive for large n. Nearly unbiased but high variance. Use for small datasets.

properties.name: Bootstrap
properties.description: Resampling method that draws samples with replacement from the original data. Used to estimate standard errors and confidence intervals.
properties.interpretation_guide: R=1000 or more bootstrap samples recommended. Useful when analytical standard errors are difficult to derive.

properties.name: Best Subset Selection
properties.description: Fit all possible models with subsets of predictors, select best by criterion (AIC, BIC, Cp, adjusted R²). Computationally expensive for p > 40.
properties.interpretation_guide: BIC tends to select smaller models than AIC. Use cross-validation for final model selection.

properties.name: Forward Stepwise Selection
properties.description: Start with null model, add predictor that most improves fit at each step. Less computationally expensive than best subset.
properties.interpretation_guide: May miss best model but computationally feasible for large p. Greedy algorithm.

properties.name: Backward Stepwise Selection
properties.description: Start with full model, remove least significant predictor at each step until stopping criterion is met.
properties.interpretation_guide: Requires n > p. May produce different results than forward selection.

properties.name: Ridge Regression (L2 Regularization)
properties.description: Adds penalty λΣβⱼ² to RSS. Shrinks coefficients toward zero but never exactly zero. Good for multicollinearity.
properties.interpretation_guide: λ=0 gives OLS. Larger λ = more shrinkage. Use CV to select λ. Coefficients are biased but lower variance.

properties.name: Lasso (L1 Regularization)
properties.description: Adds penalty λΣ|βⱼ| to RSS. Can shrink coefficients exactly to zero, performing variable selection.
properties.interpretation_guide: Performs automatic variable selection. Use when you expect many irrelevant predictors. λ selected by CV.

properties.name: Elastic Net
properties.description: Combines L1 and L2 penalties: λ[(1-α)Σβⱼ²/2 + αΣ|βⱼ|]. α controls mix (0=ridge, 1=lasso).
properties.interpretation_guide: Good when predictors are correlated (lasso may arbitrarily select one). Tune both λ and α.

properties.name: Principal Components Regression (PCR)
properties.description: Reduce predictors to M principal components, then regress Y on those components. Unsupervised dimension reduction followed by regression.
properties.interpretation_guide: Components chosen to maximize variance in X, not necessarily related to Y. M selected by CV.

properties.name: Partial Least Squares (PLS)
properties.description: Similar to PCR but components are chosen to maximize covariance with Y. Supervised dimension reduction.
properties.interpretation_guide: Often outperforms PCR when goal is prediction. First component is direction most correlated with Y.

properties.name: Logistic Regression
properties.description: Classification method modeling P(Y=1|X) using logistic function. Coefficients interpreted as log-odds ratios.
properties.interpretation_guide: exp(β) is the odds ratio. Assumes linear decision boundary. Use for binary or multinomial outcomes.

properties.name: Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA)
properties.description: Classification assuming each class has Gaussian distribution with shared covariance matrix. Estimates class priors and means.
properties.interpretation_guide: More stable than logistic regression when classes are well-separated. Assumes equal covariance across classes.

properties.name: Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA)
properties.description: Like LDA but allows each class to have its own covariance matrix. More flexible but more parameters to estimate.
properties.interpretation_guide: Better when class covariances truly differ. Requires more data per class. Quadratic decision boundary.

properties.name: Naive Bayes Classifier
properties.description: Assumes conditional independence of predictors given class. Despite naive assumption, often works well in practice.
properties.interpretation_guide: Very fast, scales well. Good baseline. Works surprisingly well for text classification.

properties.name: K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
properties.description: Non-parametric method: classify based on majority vote of K nearest neighbors. Can also be used for regression (average of neighbors).
properties.interpretation_guide: Small K = flexible (low bias, high variance). Large K = smooth (high bias, low variance). Scale predictors first.

properties.name: Decision Tree (CART)
properties.description: Recursive binary splitting of predictor space. Interpretable but prone to overfitting. Basis for ensemble methods.
properties.r_syntax:
library(rpart); rpart(y ~ ., data)
library(tree); tree(y ~ ., data)
properties.interpretation_guide: Easy to interpret and visualize. Prune using cross-validation to avoid overfitting. High variance.

properties.name: Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregating)
properties.description: Average predictions from many trees, each trained on bootstrap sample. Reduces variance of decision trees.
properties.r_syntax: library(randomForest); randomForest(y ~ ., data, mtry=p) # mtry=p means bagging
properties.interpretation_guide: Out-of-bag (OOB) error is unbiased estimate of test error. No need for separate test set.

properties.name: Random Forest
properties.description: Bagging with random feature selection at each split. Decorrelates trees, reducing variance further.
properties.r_syntax:
library(randomForest); randomForest(y ~ ., data, mtry=sqrt(p)) # classification
randomForest(y ~ ., data, mtry=p/3) # regression
properties.interpretation_guide: mtry=√p for classification, p/3 for regression. Variable importance available. Hard to overfit with more trees.

properties.name: Gradient Boosting
properties.description: Sequentially fit trees to residuals, slowly learning. Each tree is small (weak learner). Powerful but can overfit.
properties.r_syntax: library(gbm); gbm(y ~ ., data, distribution='gaussian', n.trees=5000, shrinkage=0.01)
properties.interpretation_guide: Shrinkage (learning rate) controls overfitting. Smaller shrinkage = more trees needed. Use CV for n.trees.

properties.name: XGBoost
properties.description: Optimized gradient boosting with regularization, parallel processing, and handling of missing values. State-of-the-art for tabular data.
properties.interpretation_guide: Tune: max_depth, eta (learning rate), subsample, colsample_bytree. Use early_stopping_rounds.

properties.name: Support Vector Machine (SVM)
properties.description: Find hyperplane that maximizes margin between classes. Kernel trick allows non-linear boundaries.
properties.interpretation_guide: Cost controls bias-variance tradeoff. Kernel options: linear, polynomial, radial (RBF). Scale predictors first.

properties.name: Kernel Functions
properties.definition: Functions that compute inner products in high-dimensional feature space without explicit transformation. Common kernels: linear, polynomial, radial basis function (RBF).
properties.interpretation_guide: RBF kernel is most flexible and common default. Polynomial kernel for known polynomial relationship.

properties.name: K-Means Clustering
properties.description: Partition n observations into K clusters by minimizing within-cluster sum of squares. Iteratively assigns points and updates centroids.
properties.interpretation_guide: Use nstart>1 to avoid local minima. Choose K with elbow plot or silhouette score. Scale variables first.

properties.name: Hierarchical Clustering
properties.description: Build tree of clusters by iteratively merging (agglomerative) or splitting (divisive). No need to specify K in advance.
properties.interpretation_guide: Linkage methods: complete (max distance), single (min), average, Ward. Dendrogram shows cluster hierarchy.

properties.name: Linkage Methods for Hierarchical Clustering
properties.definition: Methods to measure distance between clusters: Complete (maximum pairwise), Single (minimum), Average, Ward (minimize within-cluster variance).
properties.interpretation_guide: Complete linkage tends to produce compact clusters. Single linkage can produce chaining. Ward often gives best results.

properties.name: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
properties.description: Linear dimensionality reduction finding orthogonal directions of maximum variance. First PC explains most variance, second is orthogonal and explains next most, etc.
properties.interpretation_guide: Always scale variables. Scree plot shows variance explained by each PC. Biplot shows both scores and loadings.

properties.name: Scree Plot
properties.definition: Plot of variance explained vs. number of principal components. Used to choose number of components by looking for elbow.
properties.interpretation_guide: Keep components before the elbow where curve flattens. Alternatively, keep components explaining >80% cumulative variance.

properties.name: Confusion Matrix
properties.definition: Table showing True Positives, False Positives, True Negatives, False Negatives for a classifier.
properties.interpretation_guide: Accuracy = (TP+TN)/n. Precision = TP/(TP+FP). Recall = TP/(TP+FN). F1 = 2*Precision*Recall/(Precision+Recall).

properties.name: ROC Curve and AUC
properties.definition: Receiver Operating Characteristic curve plots True Positive Rate vs False Positive Rate at various thresholds. AUC (Area Under Curve) summarizes overall performance.
properties.interpretation_guide: AUC = 0.5 is random guessing. AUC > 0.8 is good. AUC > 0.9 is excellent. Useful when classes are imbalanced.

properties.name: Mean Squared Error (MSE)
properties.definition: Average of squared differences between predicted and actual values: MSE = Σ(yᵢ - ŷᵢ)²/n
properties.interpretation_guide: Lower is better. RMSE = √MSE is in original units. Sensitive to outliers.

properties.name: R-Squared (Coefficient of Determination)
properties.definition: Proportion of variance in Y explained by the model: R² = 1 - RSS/TSS
properties.interpretation_guide: Ranges 0-1 for training data. Can be negative for test data if model is worse than mean. Adjusted R² penalizes complexity.

properties.name: AIC and BIC
properties.definition: Model selection criteria balancing fit and complexity. AIC = -2logL + 2p. BIC = -2logL + p*log(n). Lower is better.
properties.interpretation_guide: BIC penalizes complexity more, tends to select simpler models. Use for model comparison, not absolute fit.

properties.name: Mallows' Cp
properties.definition: Model selection criterion: Cp = (RSS + 2dσ̂²)/n where d is number of predictors. Estimates test MSE.
properties.interpretation_guide: Good models have Cp close to d+1. Large Cp indicates overfitting.

properties.name: Splines (Regression Splines)
properties.description: Piecewise polynomial functions with continuity constraints at knots. More flexible than polynomials, less prone to boundary issues.
properties.r_syntax:
library(splines); lm(y ~ bs(x, df=6)) # B-spline
lm(y ~ ns(x, df=4)) # Natural spline
properties.interpretation_guide: df controls flexibility. Natural splines are linear at boundaries (more stable). Place knots at quantiles.

properties.name: Generalized Additive Models (GAM)
properties.description: Extend linear models allowing non-linear functions of each predictor while maintaining additivity: Y = α + f₁(X₁) + f₂(X₂) + ...
properties.r_syntax: library(mgcv); gam(y ~ s(x1) + s(x2) + x3, data)
properties.interpretation_guide: s() fits smooth function. Can mix smooth and linear terms. Interpretable like linear models but more flexible.

properties.name: Local Regression (LOESS/LOWESS)
properties.description: Fit weighted regression at each point using nearby observations. Span parameter controls smoothness.
properties.interpretation_guide: Span in (0,1]: smaller = more flexible. Not easily extendable to many predictors (curse of dimensionality).

properties.name: Curse of Dimensionality
properties.definition: As dimensions increase, data becomes increasingly sparse. Distance-based methods suffer because all points become equidistant in high dimensions.
properties.interpretation_guide: KNN, local regression struggle with many predictors. Use dimension reduction or regularization.

properties.name: Overfitting
properties.definition: Model fits training data too closely, capturing noise rather than signal. Results in poor generalization to new data.
properties.interpretation_guide: Signs: training error much lower than test error. Solutions: regularization, cross-validation, simpler models, more data.

properties.name: Underfitting
properties.definition: Model is too simple to capture underlying patterns. Both training and test error are high.
properties.interpretation_guide: Solutions: more complex model, add features, polynomial terms, interactions.

properties.name: glmnet
properties.purpose: Lasso, ridge, and elastic net regularized regression. Very fast coordinate descent algorithm.

properties.name: randomForest
properties.purpose: Random forest for classification and regression. Includes variable importance measures and OOB error.

properties.name: gbm
properties.purpose: Gradient boosting machines for regression and classification.

properties.name: e1071
properties.purpose: Support vector machines (svm), naive Bayes, and other classification methods.

properties.name: mgcv
properties.purpose: Generalized additive models with automatic smoothness selection.

properties.name: pls
properties.purpose: Principal component regression (PCR) and partial least squares (PLS) regression.

properties.name: leaps
properties.purpose: Best subset selection and stepwise regression for linear models.
